chunks: 2434 - And Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar, upon them both be peace, who said:
“The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, cursed three: the one who eats his provisions alone, the one who sleeps alone in a house, and the one who rides alone in the wilderness.”

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةً: three categories of people mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.لَعَنَ: invoked condemnation upon; here indicating severe disapproval
key_terms.ٱلرَّاكِبَ: the one who rides or travels
key_terms.ٱلْفَلَاةِ: the open wilderness or desolate land

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله say about eating, sleeping, or traveling alone?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a strong discouragement of isolating oneself in situations tied to daily living and travel. It reflects an ethical teaching that companionship, shared living, and avoiding vulnerable solitude are matters of proper conduct in the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2434 - Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid narrated from Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), who said:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) cursed three: the one who eats their provisions alone, the one who sleeps alone in a house, and the one who travels alone in the wilderness."
